subject: Acme procurement: SLO questionnaire, monitoring access, and exception request
messages:
From: Lisa Miller <procurement@acme-corp.com>

Cc: Tom Alvarez <it-security@acme-corp.com>
Date: 2026-04-01T08:32:00-07:00
Subject: Request: SLO measurement & monitoring access for procurement questionnaire

Hi Neha,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. Procurement needs a short reconciliation of how Redwood measures and reports on SLOs for hosted inference — specifically uptime/latency SLOs and the monitoring/alerting model. Our questionnaire requests:

1) Exact SLO definitions (what counts as "available" for the API and how latency p50/p95/p99 are computed)
2) How measurement windows are computed and how downtime is attributed (regional vs. global)
3) What monitoring/alerting thresholds you use internally and what we can subscribe to as customers
4) How customers can view or query raw metrics or dashboards (read-only access, API endpoints, or periodic exports)
5) Process for exception requests (e.g., planned maintenance windows, SLA credits, runbooks)

Attached is our procurement questionnaire (procurement_acme_slo_questions_v3.pdf). Could you provide a written response and any supporting documents? If easier we can do a 30-min call — availability next Tue/Wed afternoon PT.

Warm regards,
Lisa Miller
Head of Procurement, Acme Corp
Attachments: procurement_acme_slo_questions_v3.pdf (application/pdf, 55KB)

- Redwood defines availability at the route level (model endpoint + region).
- We publish p50/p95/p99 latency aggregated over 1-minute buckets and computed over rolling 30-day and 7-day windows (we'll include precise formulas).

I'll send the full packet shortly.

Best,
Neha Kapoor

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-04-02T09:20:00-07:00
Subject: Redwood response: SLO measurement, monitoring, and customer access (attached)

Hi Lisa / Tom — please find our written answers attached and a short summary below. Attachment: redwood-slo-answers-acme-20260402.pdf (application/pdf, 45KB) and a CSV export example in the SLA summary workbook (redwood-sla-summary-20260331.xlsx).

Executive summary (short):
- Availability SLO: 99.95% per calendar month, measured per-route per-region. "Available" = service responds with 2xx application-level responses within 10s; we exclude customer-abused requests (ratelimited, auth failures) per contract.
- Latency SLOs: published p50/p95/p99 for token-generation endpoints. Latency is computed on server-side request/response time (start of request to final token emitted) and aggregated from 1-minute histograms into percentiles using t-digest.
- Measurement windows: rolling 30-day and calendar-month windows stored as both raw 1-min buckets and pre-aggregated percentiles. Downtime attribution is regional-first: if a region serving your traffic has an incident it counts towards region SLO; global SLO is a weighted combination based on traffic routing.
- Monitoring & alerting: our on-call and infra are alerted at internal thresholds (e.g., error rate > 0.5% sustained over 5m, p95 latency > 700ms over 3m). Customers may subscribe to read-only alert webhooks for their tenant and receive incident notifications via configured endpoints (email/slack/webhook).
- Customer access to metrics: we provide three options: (1) read-only dashboard in Redwood Console with per-route filters; (2) token-authenticated metrics API to pull raw 1-minute buckets for the past 90 days; (3) periodic CSV exports delivered via secure link. We'll include sample queries in the attachment.
- Exception handling: planned maintenance windows are communicated 72h in advance for Dedicated/Private; for Hosted we provide scheduled maintenance windows and temporary reduced capacity. SLA credit requests require a postmortem and verified metric delta; emergency exceptions (e.g., region failover) are handled by an expedited review and may require contractual amendment for recurring exceptions.

Action items / attachments:
- redwood-slo-answers-acme-20260402.pdf (full Q&A and formulas)
- redwood-sla-summary-20260331.xlsx (sample exports and column mapping)
- Sample read-only dashboard link: https://console.redwood.ai/customers/acme/slo-dashboard

Would you like a short walk-through call on Fri Apr 3 (10:00–11:00 PT) or Mon Apr 6? If you plan to request an SLA exception for a specific maintenance pattern, include the proposed exception language and timeline and we'll route to Legal/Engineering.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Principal Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood-slo-answers-acme-20260402.pdf (application/pdf, 45KB); redwood-sla-summary-20260331.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet, 28KB)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>

Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-04-02T11:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood response: SLO measurement, monitoring, and customer access (technical clarifications)

Hi Lisa — quick technical clarifications from runtime: 
- Percentiles: we compute p50/p95/p99 using t-digest over 1-minute histograms; exported percentiles are population-weighted and include only successful requests.
- Exclusions: client-side timeouts and aborted TCP connections are excluded from latency buckets when the server never received the full request payload.
- Retention: raw 1-min buckets retained 90 days; pre-aggregated 30-day rolling windows retained 12 months. If you require longer retention we can include it as an add-on.
- Alerts: customers can configure alert thresholds per-route via the Console. We also support webhooks to your incident management system.

If you want sample API queries for the metrics API I can drop a curl snippet.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Software Engineer, Runtime | Redwood Inference

From: Lisa Miller <procurement@acme-corp.com>

Cc: Tom Alvarez <it-security@acme-corp.com>, Sarah Cho <sarah.cho@acme-corp.com>

Subject: Re: Redwood response: SLO measurement, monitoring, and customer access (exception request)

Neha / Marcus — thanks for the detailed packet; the team reviewed the attachments. A couple follow-ups:

1) We need to request an exception for a recurring planned maintenance window that overlaps with our peak usage (Thu 01:00–03:00 PT weekly) for the first 3 months of onboarding while we test model integrations. Proposed language: "Redwood will notify Acme 72h in advance and will not schedule more than 4 maintenance events per month that affect Acme's primary region; credits per SLA will not apply for pre-approved maintenance events as long as advance notice is given."

2) We'd like read-only metrics API keys scoped to our account to automate our internal SLO reconciliation. Please provide the steps and an expected timeline for provisioning.

3) Please provide the DocuSign link for the standard SLA amendment/exception approval so Procurement can route internally.

If possible, we need a written response on the exception language plus the DocuSign packet by Monday Apr 6 COB PT — procurement is expediting this as part of the PO.

Thanks,
Lisa Miller
Head of Procurement, Acme Corp

Subject: Re: Redwood response: SLO measurement, monitoring, and customer access (next steps & DocuSign)

Hi Lisa — appreciate the clear ask. Next steps and commitments from our side: 

- Exception language: we can accept the proposed maintenance language with one edit to clarify "primary region" as the region(s) explicitly listed in the customer config. Lauren (cc'd) will prepare the SLA amendment with that edit and deliver a DocuSign packet by EOD Apr 05 PT for your review.
- Metrics API keys: we can provision read-only token-scoped API keys. Standard timeline: 1 business day after PO/signature. Marcus will provide curl/examples (Marcus: please attach the snippet + API endpoint to the DocuSign cover note).
- Credits: agreed — pre-approved maintenance events with 72h notice will be excluded from SLA credit calculations, documented in the amendment.

I'll route the amendment to Legal and Finance today. If you need a walkthrough, I'm available Fri Apr 3 10–11 PT or Mon Apr 6 09–11 PT — otherwise we'll proceed with the DocuSign workflow.

Thanks and talk soon,
Neha Kapoor
Principal Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
